Data Visualisation & Predictive Analytics Dashboard

Unifying exploratory data analysis and real-time regression: An interactive Streamlit dashboard featuring 6 multidimensional Plotly charts and an embedded Random Forest Regressor predicting socio-economic event likelihood.

01. The Real Problem

Analyzing global socio-economic, environmental, and PESTLE (Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental) event streams typically requires juggling separate tools for data munging, static reporting, and statistical modeling. When decision-makers explore complex indicators like intensity, relevance, and likelihood, static tables fail to convey correlations or allow speculative 'what-if' forecasting.

The goal of this project was to build a unified exploratory analytics workspace in Python that combines high-performance multi-variable filtering, dynamic charting, and real-time regression forecasting in a single accessible web interface.

02. Data Processing & Feature Pipeline

In tt.py, raw data from jsondata.json is ingested and prepared with robust cleaning steps:

tt.pyFeature Preparation & Categorical Encoding
# Handle missing values and adjust data types
df['end_year'] = pd.to_numeric(df['end_year'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)
df['intensity'] = pd.to_numeric(df['intensity'], errors='coerce').fillna(0)
df['relevance'] = pd.to_numeric(df['relevance'], errors='coerce').fillna(0)
df['likelihood'] = pd.to_numeric(df['likelihood'], errors='coerce').fillna(0)
for col in ['topic', 'sector', 'region', 'pestle', 'source', 'country']:
    df[col] = df[col].fillna('Unknown')

# Encode categorical variables for the ML model
label_encoders = {}
for column in ['topic', 'sector', 'region', 'pestle', 'source', 'country']:
    le = LabelEncoder()
    df[column + '_encoded'] = le.fit_transform(df[column].astype(str))
    label_encoders[column] = le

Seven sidebar dropdowns allow visitors to slice the dataset dynamically across End Year, Topic, Sector, Region, PESTLE, Source, and Country, with instantaneous chart rerendering.

03. 6 Verified Interactive Visualizations

The dashboard implements 6 distinct Plotly visualizations designed for deep analytical exploration:

Visualization Plotly Engine Analytical Objective
Intensity vs. Likelihood px.scatter Examines clustering and outliers between event severity and probability, color-coded by topic with tooltip title inspection.
Relevance Over Time px.line Tracks temporal trajectory of strategic importance across distinct industry domains.
Region Distribution px.pie Aggregates geographic density and event volume across continental markets.
Top 10 Topics px.bar Identifies highest-frequency risk and opportunity categories via nlargest(10) aggregation.
PESTLE Analysis px.bar Decomposes macro-environmental influences into structural categories.
Correlation Heatmap go.Heatmap (Viridis) Visualizes statistical covariance between numeric indicators (intensity, relevance, likelihood).

04. Random Forest Predictive Engine

Beyond retrospective charting, the application embeds a trained regression model to forecast the likelihood score of unseen events:

  • Model Architecture: RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=42) trained on an 80/20 train/test split.
  • Evaluation Metric: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) evaluated on the held-out test split and displayed transparently to the user.
  • Interactive Forecasting Form: Visitors adjust numeric sliders (Intensity, Relevance, Target Year) and categorical dropdowns (Sector, Region, PESTLE, Topic, Source, Country). The inputs are mapped through the fitted label_encoders and submitted to model.predict([encoded_values]), outputting the forecasted likelihood instantly.

05. Engineering Decisions & Optimization Scope

Verified Findings & Future Scope

  • In-Memory Training: The Random Forest model is trained on startup when Streamlit initializes. For rapid iteration on small datasets (~thousands of rows) this works seamlessly; for enterprise scaling, the model pipeline would be pre-serialized to a Joblib/ONNX artifact.
  • Streamlit Caching: Uses @st.cache_data to cache raw JSON ingestion, avoiding repetitive disk I/O on filter updates.
  • Defensive Parsing: Handles infinite and empty values via replace([np.inf, -np.inf, ''], np.nan).dropna() to safeguard matrix operations.
